source.title: DiaBlo: Diagonal Blocks Are Sufficient For Finetuning
source.authors: Selcuk Gurses; Ao-Zhong Zhang; Yan-Xia Deng; Xu Dong; Xin Li; Nai-Gang Wang; Peng-Hang Yin; Zi Yang

record.tranche_reason: The study presents DiaBlo as a fine-tuning method and evaluates it for safety alignment; it does not test whether fine-tuning erodes existing safety behavior or any of the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study fine-tunes models on SaferPaca to perform safety alignment, then reports refusal rates on harmful prompts. This is behavior induced toward safety, not evidence about safety erosion in an already safety-trained model. Baseline-method results in Table 3 are stated to be taken from LoRI and are not extracted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: DiaBlo is a PEFT method paper. Its safety experiment fine-tunes non-instruction-tuned base models on SaferPaca, which adds safety data, and reports HEx-PHI refusal rates to rank DiaBlo against other PEFT methods. Safety is deliberately induced. No already-aligned model is fine-tuned and measured for erosion, and there is no per-token analysis, prefilling attack, localization test or deepening test, so no version of the claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report that DiaBlo outperforms the LoRA-family baselines on HEx-PHI refusal: 97.6% on Llama3-8B and 98.8% on Mistral-7B. They draw no conclusion about safety erosion or how deep alignment goes.
record.recipe_differences: This study uses diagonal-block parameter-efficient fine-tuning on SaferPaca to train for safety alignment; it does not test harmful or benign fine-tuning as an intervention that erodes pre-existing safety.

fits_no_version.finding: DiaBlo fine-tuning on SaferPaca raises HEx-PHI refusal of base Llama3-8B and Mistral-7B. Zero-shot refusal is 78.7% and 80.5% (from LoRI); after fine-tuning it is 96–99%, above the LoRA, DoRA and LoRI figures quoted from LoRI.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-efficient safety-data fine-tuning of base models yields high refusal on HEx-PHI, varying slightly by PEFT method.

record.problems: The models are described as non-instruction-tuned, and the study does not report a before-and-after safety comparison for an already safety-trained model. The baseline-method results are taken from LoRI; no uncertainty estimates are reported for the refusal rates.
record.rows_left_out: Baseline-method results in Table 3 are stated to be taken from LoRI, so they were not extracted as results of this study.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning of a safety-trained model.
No before/after harmfulness check after benign fine-tuning (CodeAlpaca, commonsense, math) of aligned models. All models are base models.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No test of whether safety is localized in weights or ranks. The diagonal-block sufficiency results concern GSM8K only.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.
No deep-alignment training or robustness test of refusal.

record.verdict_notes: HEx-PHI from Qi et al. (an original source) is used only as an evaluation set. All baseline figures in Table 3 are taken from LoRI. No uncertainty is reported. The models are non-instruction-tuned (Appendix A.4.1).

versions.untested_parts: Whether harmful examples make a safety-trained model comply with harmful requests.
Whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign data raises harmful compliance in a safety-trained model.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes as ways to bypass refusal.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether the data or training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Whether training spreads safety beyond the first tokens and whether that persists.
